docs.title: Creamy Mapo Tofu Udon
docs.text: Serves: 2 Total Time: ~25 minutes

docs.title: Meat Mixture
docs.text:
• 200 g (7 oz) ground beef or pork
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 Tbsp minced ginger
  • 1 scallion, white and green parts separated
  • 1 Tbsp doubanjiang
  • 1 Tbsp Sichuan chili oil
  • 1 Tbsp Shaoxing wine
  • 1 tsp black vinegar
  • ½ tsp sugar
  • Pinch of salt
  • Pinch of MSG

docs.title: Tofu Cream Sauce
docs.text:
• ½ block (150 g) silken tofu
  • 1 Tbsp white miso
  • 1 Tbsp creamy peanut butter
  • 1 tsp soy sauce

docs.title: To Serve
docs.text:
• 2 portions udon noodles (~400 g)
  • Scallion greens, thinly sliced

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Prep Aromatics Mince garlic and ginger. Slice scallion whites and greens separately.

  2. Cook Meat Heat 1 Tbsp neutral oil in a wok or skillet over medium-high. Add the ground beef or pork and cook until browned and slightly crisp. Remove and set aside, leaving some fat in the pan.

  3. Build the Mapo Base Lower heat to medium. Add garlic, ginger, and scallion whites; sauté about 30 seconds until fragrant. Add doubanjiang; fry 45–60 seconds until the oil turns deep red and aromatic.

  4. Deglaze and Combine Deglaze with Shaoxing wine. Add sichuan chili oil, black vinegar, sugar, salt, and MSG. Return meat to the pan, stir-fry until glossy and cohesive, about 1–2 minutes. Set aside and keep warm.

  5. Make the Tofu Cream Sauce In a blender, combine silken tofu, miso, peanut butter, and soy sauce. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. Taste and adjust seasoning — it should be savory and nutty.

  6. Cook Udon Boil udon according to package directions. Drain well.

  7. Assemble

    1. Add udon noodles to each bowl.
    2. Spoon the hot meat mixture over the noodles.
    3. Pour the tofu cream sauce over top — let it flow naturally between the meat and noodles.
    4. Finish with scallion greens.

  8. To Eat Mix everything together just before eating so the tofu cream coats the noodles and meat evenly.

docs.title: Lahmacun (1.5 lb Ground Beef) — With Homemade Dough, Baked on a Sheet Pan
Dough (8–10 thin rounds)
docs.text:
• Warm water: 1 cup (240 g)
  • Instant yeast: 1.5 tsp (5 g)
  • Sugar: 1 tsp (4 g)
  • Bread/AP flour: 3 cups (360 g)
  • Salt: 1.5 tsp (9 g)
  • Olive oil: 1 tbsp (15 g)

docs.title: Meat Topping (food-processor method, no crushed tomato)
docs.text:
• Ground beef: 1.5 lb (680 g)
  • Onion: 1 medium (~150 g)
  • Garlic: 3 cloves (~12 g)
  • Red bell pepper: 1 small (~120 g)
  • Flat-leaf parsley: 1 cup packed (~40 g)
  • Tomato paste: 3 tbsp (50 g)
  • Red pepper paste (optional): 1 tbsp (20 g)
  • Olive oil: 2 tbsp (30 g)
  • Paprika: 2 tsp (4 g)
  • Aleppo pepper: 2 tsp (4 g)
  • Cumin: 1 tsp (2 g)
  • Salt: 15 g
  • Black pepper: 1 tsp (2 g)
  • Water: 2–4 tbsp, as needed for spreadability

docs.title: Garnish
docs.text:
• Lemon wedges
  • Onion–parsley–sumac salad
  • Pickled peppers (optional)

docs.title: 1. Make the Dough
docs.text:
1. Mix warm water, yeast, sugar. Rest 5 min.
  2. Add flour, salt, olive oil. Knead 8–10 min until smooth.
  3. Cover and rise 1 hour until doubled.
  4. Divide into 8–10 balls; rest 15 min.

docs.title: 2. Make the Topping (Food Processor)
docs.text:
1. In the processor: onion chunks, garlic, bell pepper → pulse to a fine mince, not a puree.
  2. Add parsley → quick pulses to incorporate.
  3. Move veg mix to a bowl.
  4. Add ground beef, tomato paste, red pepper paste, olive oil, paprika, Aleppo, cumin, salt, pepper.
  5. Mix thoroughly. Add 2–4 tbsp water to achieve a smooth, spreadable consistency.

docs.title: 3. Shape the Bases
docs.text:
1. Preheat oven to 475°F (246°C). Place your sheet pan inside to preheat optional but recommended for crisper bottoms.
  2. Roll each dough ball very thin—about 10–11 in (25–28 cm) diameter. You want almost tortilla-thin.

docs.title: 4. Assemble
docs.text:
1. Lay parchment on the hot sheet pan (or use a room-temp sheet pan if easier).
  2. Place one rolled dough round on parchment.
  3. Spread a thin, even layer of topping, edge-to-edge. Press it in.

docs.title: 5. Bake
docs.text:
1. Bake 6–9 minutes until edges blister and topping is cooked.
  2. Remove and repeat. Rotate pan if browning unevenly.

docs.title: 6. Serve
docs.text:
• Squeeze lemon.
  • Add onion–parsley–sumac salad.
  • Roll and eat immediately.

docs.title: Loco Moco
docs.text: Serves: 4 Total Time: ~35 minutes

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 3 cups rice
  • 4 burger patties

docs.title: Gravy
docs.text:
• 3 Tbsp unsalted butter (42 g)
  • 3 Tbsp all-purpose flour (24 g)
  • 2 cups beef stock (480 ml)
  • 1 Tbsp soy sauce
  • 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce
  • ½ tsp onion powder
  • ½ tsp garlic powder
  • Fresh black pepper to taste

docs.title: To Serve
docs.text: • 4 eggs, crispy fried

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Cook the Rice Start rice in the cooker so it’s ready when the rest is done.

  2. Make the Gravy

    1. Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
    2. Stir in flour; cook 2–3 minutes until golden and nutty.
    3. Gradually whisk in beef stock.
    4. Add soy, Worcestershire, onion powder, garlic powder, and pepper.
    5. Simmer until thick and glossy. Adjust seasoning.

  3. Grill burgers Pull at 150.

  4. Fry the Eggs Cook crispy-fried.

  5. Assemble In each bowl: rice → burger → ladle of gravy → fried egg. Garnish with scallions and furikake or togarashi.
